java_locations.role: Tries SequenceDiagramFactory, ClassDiagramFactory, ActivityDiagramFactory, DescriptionDiagramFactory and later UML factories in order, accepting the first factory that consumes the complete source without producing PSystemError.

A command factory remains a candidate only while every input command is recognized and executes successfully; an unconsumed direction line rejects that factory rather than contributing a weaker score.
Registers sequence participants, arrows, notes and common commands, but does not register CommandRankDir.

Defines rank direction as left%s to%s right or top%s to%s bottom with exactly one Pattern2 whitespace at each internal separator, one-or-more whitespace before direction, and Pattern2 case-insensitive matching.
Defines the complete case-insensitive Sequence grouping inventory, including optional parallel prefix, opt/alt/loop/par/par2/break/critical/else/end/also/group/partition, colors and comments.
Accepts optional @ and optional labels, including colon-separated labels, while later graph factories register only the bare Description CommandNewpage form.

Owns the lifecycle, grouping-adjacent, spacing, pagination, numbering, reference and footbox grammar variants omitted by the first Rust prefix inventory. Pattern2 makes these command regexes case-insensitive.
Registers CommandRankDir. Mixed DESCRIPTION leaves such as database or queue still reject this earlier candidate unless allowmixing has enabled their creation.
Registers CommandRankDir together with DESCRIPTION declarations and links, so shared sequence/deployment words remain consumable here after Sequence and an ineligible Class candidate have failed.

rust_locations.role: The first follow-up excludes Sequence for two exact lowercase rank-direction strings and uses a manually selected prefix list for Sequence-only commands. It misses valid case and whitespace forms and registered command families, and conflates shared grammar variants such as bare versus labeled newpage.
Already owns the concrete Sequence command grammar and distinctions needed for a typed factory-line classifier, but dispatch currently duplicates a narrower inventory in parse/mod.rs.

claimed_invariant: For an @startuml source containing a complete Java CommandRankDir line, SequenceDiagramFactory is not viable because its registered inventory has no CommandRankDir. The valid command is case-insensitive, uses exactly one Pattern2 whitespace at each internal direction separator, and permits one-or-more whitespace before the final direction keyword. Remaining factories are tried in Java order and may consume shared declarations, links, common commands, bare newpage, bare/hide/show footbox and ordinary notes. A line whose exact grammar variant is owned only by Sequence, including participant/order forms, lifecycle commands, short activation, grouping, box, divider, delay, hspace, autonumber, autoactivate, return, ref, labeled/@ newpage, ignore/autonewpage, footbox on/off and sequence-only note/message forms, cannot be laundered through a permissive later parser; rank direction plus any such line yields no viable factory.
causal_divergence: Rust originally treated subtype selection as unrestricted score maximization. The first correction separated Sequence viability but recognized rank direction only as two exact lowercase strings and hand-enumerated selected Sequence-only prefixes in parse/mod.rs. The adversarial review showed both halves under-model Java: mixed case and legal extra whitespace before direction leave Sequence eligible, while omitted registered commands such as grouping, divider, delay, autonewpage, short activation, lifecycle and labeled newpage are silently discarded by later Rust parsers. Keyword-level categories also lose grammar distinctions: later factories consume bare newpage and bare/hide/show footbox, but not Sequence's labeled/@ newpage or footbox on/off variants. The defect is duplicated, incomplete command ownership rather than an insufficient score adjustment.
planned_model_change: Move Sequence factory-line ownership into sequence.rs as a typed classifier returning not-sequence, shared-with-later, or sequence-only with a command-family identity. Derive it from the same grammar helpers used by SeqParser where those helpers exist, and cover the remaining registered Java commands with cited complete regex forms rather than prefixes. Add a Java-compatible rank-direction classifier in parse/mod.rs that preserves exact internal separator cardinality, case-insensitivity and final one-or-more whitespace. detect_uml_subtype will exclude Sequence on a valid rank-direction command and return Unconsumable only when the typed classifier finds a Sequence-only grammar variant; shared variants continue to later family scoring. Malformed rank-direction attempts remain unconsumable instead of being ignored.

alt/loop/par2/also grouping, divider, ASCII and Unicode delay, hspace, autonewpage and autonumber inc

acceptance: The preserved checker_06 source selects Deployment/DESCRIPTION on the no-oracle path and retains its entities and relation.
Fresh shared-keyword sources with either direction and varied declaration order select the same Java family without relying on label spelling.
A direction-only source and a direction plus weak ordinary arrow do not select Sequence.
The complete typed Sequence-only inventory plus a rank-direction command returns a parser error rather than being made valid by a later permissive parser.
Mixed-case rank direction and legal final whitespace eliminate Sequence, while doubled internal separators remain invalid.
Bare newpage, bare/hide/show footbox, hide/show unlinked, common commands and ordinary notes remain available to later factories; labeled/@ newpage and footbox on/off do not.
Unrelated sources without a rank-direction command retain their existing subtype selection.
An independent checker attacks command order, shared keywords, later-factory continuation and invalid mixed grammars.
forbidden_approaches: adding arbitrary Deployment score to offset Sequence
special-casing Unicode, checker labels or the database-plus-queue fixture shape
using rendered SVG differences as the subtype classifier
forcing every source containing a direction command to Deployment or Class
changing the command parsers to accept syntax solely to make the selected family succeed
declared_residue: This correction models the complete registered Sequence-only intersection exposed by CommandRankDir; general command-by-command viability between every pair of later UML factories remains broader work.
Rust splits Java DescriptionDiagramFactory into Component, UseCase and Deployment models, so selection among those Rust subtypes continues to use existing semantic evidence.
Unicode UGroup metadata serialization and repeated left-to-right unresolved-edge paint suppression are separate mechanisms from factory consumability.
